q.en: In "The confident student answered quickly," what part of speech is "confident"?
q.bn: "The confident student answered quickly" বাক্যে "confident" কোন parts of speech?

why.en: "Confident" describes the noun "student," so it's an adjective.
why.bn: "Confident" noun "student"-কে describe করছে, তাই এটা adjective।

q.en: In the same sentence, what part of speech is "quickly"?
q.bn: একই বাক্যে "quickly" কোন parts of speech?

why.en: "Quickly" describes the verb "answered" — that's an adverb's job.
why.bn: "Quickly" verb "answered"-কে describe করছে — এটাই adverb-এর কাজ।

q.en: Which sentence has correct English word order?

why.en: English puts the verb right after the subject (Subject-Verb-Object): I (S) study (V) English (O).
why.bn: English-এ verb বসে subject-এর ঠিক পরে (Subject-Verb-Object): I (S) study (V) English (O)।

why.en: "Smiled" doesn't act on anything, so there's no object — just Subject + Verb.
why.bn: "Smiled" কোনো কিছুর উপর act করছে না, তাই object নেই — শুধু Subject + Verb।

q.en: Bangla sentences typically put the verb...

options.en: right after the subject, like English
at the very end of the sentence
at the very start of the sentence

why.en: Bangla is Subject-Object-Verb (verb last); English is Subject-Verb-Object (verb in the middle) — this is the biggest word-order difference between the two languages.
why.bn: বাংলা হলো Subject-Object-Verb (verb শেষে); English হলো Subject-Verb-Object (verb মাঝখানে) — এটাই দুই ভাষার সবচেয়ে বড় word-order পার্থক্য।
